interest: Covers pre-WWII US monitoring of suspected Japanese espionage in Venezuela, including commercial fronts and coded telegrams routed via Venezuelan radio.
overview: This file compiles U.S. State Department correspondence, consular despatches, diplomatic instructions, intelligence memorandums, and confidential informant reports from 1931 to 1939 regarding alleged Japanese espionage, hydrographic surveys, and clandestine activities in Venezuela. Initial investigations in 1931–1932 focused on a party of Japanese fishermen arriving via the French liner Flandre at La Guaira with motor launches, whom American consular officials and the Office of Naval Intelligence suspected of conducting clandestine water soundings along the Venezuelan coast and towards Colombia. Subsequent records from 1938 examine resident Japanese commercial agents in Caracas, including Seijiro Yazawa and traveling representative Sotochi Hara, who were suspected of gathering coastal intelligence, photographing Lake Maracaibo oil installations, and negotiating petroleum trade agreements. The file concludes in 1939 with reports from an American radio executive alerting Secretary of State Cordell Hull to unusually high volumes of coded radiograms sent by the Japanese mission in Caracas to Tokyo, suspected of relaying intelligence gathered around the U.S. Canal Zone in Panama.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of consular correspondence concerning the arrival and activities of Japanese fishermen along the Venezuelan coast.
subfiles.from: Warden McK. Wilson, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Legation, Caracas
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 638: Chargé Wilson forwards Vice Consul reports on newly arrived Japanese fishermen along Venezuela's coast, noting no clear sign yet of ulterior motives.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 638 from Caracas on Japanese Fishermen in Venezuela
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Inquiry from Vice Consul Mokma regarding newspaper reports of Japanese fishing vessels potentially taking coastal water soundings.
subfiles.from: Gerald A. Mokma, American Vice Consul, Maracaibo
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Mokma asks Matthews about Japanese fishermen near La Guaira, suspecting their large equipped boats could be surveying coastal depths.
subfiles.title: Letter from Vice Consul Mokma to Vice Consul Matthews on Japanese Fishing Operations
subfiles.to: Ben C. Matthews, American Vice Consul, La Guaira

subfiles.about: Consular report confirming the arrival of thirteen Japanese nationals and motor launches at La Guaira aboard the French liner Flandre.
subfiles.from: Ben C. Matthews, American Vice Consul, La Guaira
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Matthews reports twelve Japanese men and a woman arrived at La Guaira in October 1931 with fishing and sounding equipment, then moved on to Higuerote.
subfiles.title: Letter from Vice Consul Matthews to Vice Consul Mokma on Japanese Arrival and Movements
subfiles.to: Gerald A. Mokma, American Vice Consul, Maracaibo

subfiles.about: Report on the movements of the Japanese fishing party along the coast to Higuerote and police surveillance over suspected soundings.
subfiles.from: Warden McK. Wilson, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Legation, Caracas
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 653: Wilson confirms the Japanese fishermen took coastal soundings as far as Higuerote, drawing local suspicion and police surveillance despite no confirmed espionage.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 653 from Caracas on Coastal Soundings and Surveillance of Japanese Fishermen
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: State Department instruction directing a discreet investigation into the Japanese fishermen at the request of Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.from: Francis White, For the Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 167 directs the Caracas Legation to investigate the Japanese fishermen's ship, route, and equipment at the Navy's request, using discreet consular cooperation.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 167 to Caracas Requesting Investigation for Naval Intelligence
subfiles.to: George T. Summerlin, American Minister, Caracas

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum summarizing the file on Japanese fishermen taking soundings along the Venezuelan coast.
subfiles.from: J. B. Faust, Division of Latin-American Affairs
subfiles.summary: Faust summarizes despatches on the thirteen Japanese fishermen and their soundings, noting Venezuelan officials continue watching them while the fishing and surveying continue unhindered.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum by J. B. Faust on Japanese Fishing File
subfiles.to: Edwin C. Wilson, Division of Latin-American Affairs

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording a conference with the Director of Naval Intelligence regarding Japanese intelligence operations in Mexico, Venezuela, and Colombia.
subfiles.from: Edwin C. Wilson, Division of Latin-American Affairs
subfiles.summary: Wilson records ONI's Captain Ellis urging tracing of the fishermen's steamer through the Panama Canal and alerting Bogotá and Central America to watch for them along Colombia's coast.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum by Edwin C. Wilson on Naval Intelligence Concerns
subfiles.to: Department of State Files / Colleagues

subfiles.about: Report that the Japanese fishing venture has failed financially and members have dispersed into agriculture and domestic work.
subfiles.from: George T. Summerlin, American Minister, Caracas
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 698: Summerlin reports the Japanese fishing venture at La Guaira collapsed from debt, its launches seized, and the men dispersed with no evidence of espionage found.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 698 from Caracas on Collapse of Fishing Enterprise and Dispersion of Japanese
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Letter to Naval Intelligence reporting on Japanese activities in La Guaira, lavish spending, and an attempt to secure an agricultural concession.
subfiles.from: Mack H. Olsen, New York, N.Y. (writing from Curaçao)
subfiles.summary: Olsen reports to Naval Intelligence that well-funded Japanese fishermen in La Guaira sought a rice-plantation concession, which President Gómez opposed.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mack H. Olsen to Director of Naval Intelligence on 'Japs in Venezuela'
subfiles.to: Director of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Instruction transmitting a copy of Mack H. Olsen's letter regarding Japanese activities in Venezuela to the Legation at Caracas.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 191 forwards Mack Olsen's April 1932 letter on Japanese fishermen to the Caracas Legation for its files.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 191 to Caracas Transmitting Olsen Intelligence Letter
subfiles.to: George T. Summerlin, American Minister, Caracas

subfiles.about: Internal State Department note identifying Henry Shumacher as the individual legally challenging Venezuelan oil titles.
subfiles.summary: Division note identifies Henry Shumacher, mentioned regarding Japanese fishermen, as likely Harry A. Schumacher, who was contesting Venezuelan oil titles.
subfiles.title: Division Memorandum on the Identity of Henry Shumacher
subfiles.to: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Despatch No. 915 regarding stationary Japanese intelligence agents in Caracas.
subfiles.summary: Memo notes reliable reports of stationary Japanese espionage agents in Caracas aided by monthly NYK shipping calls, though Venezuela remains firmly anti-Japanese.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum by MRM on Japanese Agents in Caracas
subfiles.to: Laurence Duggan, Chief, Division of the American Republics

subfiles.about: Report on suspected stationary Japanese intelligence agents in Caracas, commercial networks, and past coastal sounding activities.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 915: Nicholson reports Seijiro Yazawa, Caracas's Japanese colony head, as a suspected espionage director who financed 1928 fishermen soundings at several ports; Venezuela's government remains opposed to Japanese influence.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 915 from Caracas on Stationary Japanese Secret Agents
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Brief division note regarding Japanese shipping expansion in trade between Germany and the Americas.
subfiles.from: Division of the American Republics (initialed VMM)
subfiles.summary: Brief memo flags intelligence that a Japanese shipping line may become the main carrier of trade between German ports and the Americas.
subfiles.title: Division Memorandum on Japanese Shipping Lines in Foreign Trade
subfiles.to: Laurence Duggan, Chief, Division of the American Republics

subfiles.about: Report on suspected Japanese intelligence agent Sotochi Hara investigating Lake Maracaibo oil fields under commercial cover.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 958: Nicholson reports suspected agent Sotochi Hara, posing as a textile salesman, photographed coastlines, inspected Lake Maracaibo oil fields at night, and sought Venezuelan oil sales for Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 958 from Caracas on Suspected Agent Sotochi Hara
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Despatch No. 958 reporting suspected espionage activities of Sotochi Hara in Venezuelan oil regions.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Despatch No. 958, restating that Sotochi Hara photographed coastlines, visited Lake Maracaibo oil sites at night, and sought to open Venezuelan oil sales to Japan.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Despatch No. 958 on Sotochi Hara
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 40 regarding Japanese interest in Venezuelan oil fields and diplomatic trade negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Despatch 40: notes former Japanese Consul Wakabayashi's presence in Caracas seeking to renew a bilateral trade agreement.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 40 on Japanese Oil Interest
subfiles.to: Department of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 40 regarding general observations on Japanese visitors in Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Despatch 40: records diplomatic reporting on the movements and activities of Japanese visitors in Venezuela.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 40 on Japanese Visitors
subfiles.to: Department of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 120 transmitting a memorandum of conversation with the Japanese Minister to Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Despatch 120: notes a memo of conversation between an American Legation officer and the Japanese Minister to Venezuela.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 120 on Japanese Diplomatic Talks
subfiles.to: Department of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Letter from an American radio executive alerting Secretary Hull to large volumes of coded Japanese radiograms sent via Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: Axtell alerts Secretary Hull to the Japanese mission's $6,000 monthly coded cables, theorizing Panama agents route reports to Caracas for transmission via Venezuelan radio.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. H. Axtell to Secretary Hull on Japanese Coded Communications
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Typed office duplicate of R. H. Axtell's letter exposing Japanese coded radiotelegraph relays from Caracas to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate transcript of Axtell's letter on Japanese coded radio traffic from Caracas, suggesting US cryptanalysts inspect RCA records in New York.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter from R. H. Axtell on Coded Radiotelegraph Traffic
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: State Department instruction transmitting R. H. Axtell's letter to the American Ambassador in Caracas.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 7 transmits Axtell's letter to the Caracas Ambassador for files, directing a thank-you acknowledgment if no objection exists.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 7 to Caracas Transmitting Axtell Letter
subfiles.to: American Ambassador, Caracas
